business_scope.primary_industry_name: Search Engine Optimization Data Crawler and Keyword Analytics Tool

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - English common law, Samoan customary law, and statute (International Companies Act 1987)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Samoa-China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (signed 2016, in force 2017)
PACER Plus (Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus, in force 2020)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018 (Samoa); Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2018; International Companies Act 1987 (as amended); International Companies (Amendment) Act 2015 (beneficial owner register); Samoa International Finance Authority Act 2005; Economic Substance Regulations 2019; FATF Recommendations 12 and 22

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) and each director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the country of origin of the UBO/director, followed by the competent Apostille authority of that country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Samoa acceded in 2018; in force 2 March 2019); Consular Legalization applies for issuers from non-Hague contracting states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement dated within the last 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or issuing bank of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization of the notarized copy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Banker's reference or letter of good standing for each UBO
Certificate of incorporation and register extract (good standing) of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry of the country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Registered agent Client Due Diligence Questionnaire and Certificate of Identity (executed before a SIFA-licensed registered agent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: SIFA-licensed registered agent in Samoa (with notarization in the UBO's jurisdiction)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening of all UBOs, directors, officers, and authorized signatories against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT Sanctions List, and Samoa's domestic sanctions and denied-persons lists; automated PEP database screening with mandatory Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) on any PEP match, high-risk jurisdiction flag, or adverse media hit; risk-rating considers source of funds, geographic exposure, and business industry; screening results are archived in the registered agent's AML/CFT file and retained for at least five (5) years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) - International Companies e-Registry; name clearance is lodged exclusively through a SIFA-licensed registered agent via the SAMOA IFA online lodgement portal (eRegistry)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name of an International Company must be expressed in the Latin/Roman alphabet and must end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd'. A name in another script (e.g., Chinese) may be approved only as a secondary or translated name where a Roman-alphabet transliteration and an English translation are concurrently submitted and approved by SIFA; the filed Memorandum and Articles remain in English or include an English translation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant (through its SIFA-licensed registered agent) may: (1) request a written statement of reasons from SIFA within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice; (2) submit a formal administrative appeal and, where practicable, a revised alternative name within 21 calendar days of the statement of reasons; (3) if refused, apply to the Registrar for binding administrative review under the International Companies Act 1987; and (4) file an originating summons for judicial review before the Supreme Court of Samoa within 28 calendar days of the final administrative refusal. A fresh name-reservation application for the alternative name is recommended simultaneously to preserve priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible in substance but not in form. The statutory registered office of the International Company must be the physical office of a SIFA-licensed registered agent in Samoa, where the statutory registers (including the beneficial owner register) and service-of-process records are maintained. A virtual office or domiciliation-only address cannot serve as the registered office. For this license-free MarTech/analytics SaaS holding model, no physical staff, assets, premises, or economic nexus in Samoa is required; the entity qualifies as a non-tax-resident offshore International Company under the International Companies Act 1987 and is outside the scope of Samoa's Economic Substance Regulations 2019 for its foreign-source SaaS activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low - estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection at the registered office of between 1% and 5% (baseline point estimate 3%) for a low AML-risk, license-free ISIC 6201 data-crawler/analytics SaaS holding entity with a compliant SIFA-licensed agent, no local subsidy claims, and no sanctions or adverse-media flags. Probability increases to 10-15% upon the occurrence of a PEP involvement, UBO filing default, sanctions hit, or the use of a sensitive name token.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: SIFA administrative fee schedule and prevailing registered-agent tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration fee under the International Companies Act 1987 fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Year-1 annual government license fee (prepaid at incorporation)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual license and tax-exemption fee per SIFA published tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: SIFA-licensed registered agent service (registered office, statutory registers, UBO register maintenance, government liaison)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for low-risk offshore International Companies (USD 750-1,000 per annum)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT client due diligence, PEP and sanctions screening, and risk-rating fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: AML compliance cost under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2018; market benchmark per UBO

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed legal drafting fee; prevailing market benchmark for bilingual offshore incorporation documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: International courier and e-filing handling charges
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Courier provider and registered agent disbursements

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended, ss. 4, 6-9 (incorporation procedure), s. 12 (share capital), s. 22 (registered office), ss. 26-31 (directors and officers); International Companies (Fees) Regulations; Mutual Funds Act and AML/CFT (Amendment) Act 2020 for record-keeping standards
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 (Application for Incorporation) together with the Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital requirement. An International Company may be incorporated with nil issued capital or unpaid shares; no escrow account, capital deposit, or bank reference requirement is imposed by the Registrar (ICA s. 12)
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company be incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987, and that the registered agent be and is hereby authorized to sign and file the Memorandum and Articles of Association and Form 1 with the Registrar of International Companies. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the subscription of one ordinary share be accepted, the share be issued as fully paid, and the registered office be established at the registered agent’s Apia address. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the nominated individuals be appointed as first directors, that [Name] be appointed Secretary, and that the directors be authorized to open bank accounts, approve a share certificate form, and take all actions required to commence business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), via licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct a SIFA-licensed registered agent to submit a name clearance request with three proposed names in order of preference. The agent checks the International Companies Register for identical or confusingly similar names, as well as prohibited names under the Companies Act and International Companies Act. Approved names are reserved for up to 30 days; the name must include a permissible corporate identifier such as 'Limited' or 'Ltd'.
required_dossiers: Corporate profile and intended business description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or reserved by another entity, the agent submits an alternative name from the initial list or files a written requisition to the Registrar seeking administrative review; a Form 1 can be resubmitted within the 30-day reservation window without fresh fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed registered agent in Samoa, acting as notarizing officer for certified copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent drafts the Memorandum and Articles of Association (including objects clause for software/SaaS services, share structure, director appointment mechanics) and the Form 1 application. The agent certifies and notarizes identity documents, obtains signed consent to act from the first directors, and verifies the registered office address at the agent's Apia office.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of passport of each director/shareholder
Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement, dated within 3 months)
Consent to act forms for first directors and secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the objects clause, capital structure, or director residency declarations, the agent files a curative amendment to the Memorandum and Articles and resubmits; no penalty applies for corrections made within 14 days of the query notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Filing and Payment of Official Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent submits the signed Form 1, executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, and supporting documents to SIFA via the online filing portal or physical lodgment at SIFA offices in Apia. The official state incorporation fee of USD 100 (standard authorized capital up to USD 1,000,000) and any agent service fee are paid by bank transfer or SIFA cashier; a fee receipt is issued for the file.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
Consent to act forms and certified identity documents
Proof of payment of incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is rejected due to defects (e.g., missing consent or incomplete attestation), the Registrar issues a written requisition listing deficiencies; the agent cures and refiles within 14 calendar days without re-payment of the official fee. Persistent rejection due to name conflict requires a fresh name clearance under Step 1.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Entry into the Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon validation of the Form 1 and constitutional documents, the Registrar enters the company in the International Companies Register and issues the Certificate of Incorporation under the official seal, together with a certified copy of the registered Memorandum and Articles. The certificate evidences the creation of a legal person with limited liability effective from the date of issue.
required_dossiers: No additional dossiers required; reliance on the approved Form 1 and constitutional documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains a clerical error (wrong name, date, or capital), the registered agent petitions the Registrar for rectification of the register under ICA s. 15; the Registrar issues an amended certificate, typically within 2 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors, Registered Agent, and licensed banking/corporate service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting to adopt the First Board Resolution, allot the subscribed share, approve the form of share certificate, open the registered office records (register of directors, members, charges), and pass a banking resolution. The company then opens a corporate bank account or payment-rail account (Stripe/Paddle) using the Certificate of Incorporation and governance documents; any beneficial ownership particulars are filed with SIFA as required under the AML/CFT (Amendment) Act 2020.
required_dossiers: Passport and proof of address of all signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank or payment-rail due diligence questions the corporate record, the agent supplies an apostilled certificate of good standing and certified board resolutions; any discrepancy in the share register is cured by an internal corrective resolution and updated register filing with SIFA.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for a pure software/SaaS data analytics service; no industrial manufacturing, mining, or processing authority is engaged. Administrative supervision rests with the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) for general commercial conduct and registration.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No separate industry operating license or business-activity permit is required for ISIC 6201 (computer programming/SEO analytics software) under Samoan law; the Certificate of Incorporation and standard commercial registration constitute sufficient authorization to operate the cloud-based SEO content analytics tool.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA), Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Fully virtual cloud service with no construction, land disturbance, discharge, or natural resource extraction; no EIA registration or environmental permit required under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — the service produces no wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste streams. If a leased office operates, it must comply with the Samoa Water Authority trade-waste discharge limits for sanitary sewage and the Apia municipal solid waste collection requirements; server hosting and data processing are outsourced to third-party cloud providers with their own environmental compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Leased office premises must obtain a fire safety clearance from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA), covering fire extinguishers, smoke detection, and evacuation plans; workplace conditions must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2011 administered by the MCIL Labour Division, including electrical safety inspection and first-aid provisions. No factory or heavy-structure load inspection is triggered by this SaaS activity; a building occupancy certificate issued by PUMA/MNRE is required only if structural alterations are made.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue of Samoa (Maota o Tupe Lafo) – Revenue Information Management System (RIMS) / e-Services portal at www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Samoa International Company applies via the registered agent using form IR-1 together with the certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles, certificate of compliance, and a resolution appointing the registered agent; the Ministry for Revenue issues a Tax Identification Number (TIN) and a tax exemption certificate under the International Companies Act 1987 and the Income Tax Act 2015.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election. The International Company automatically receives a statutory tax exemption certificate for offshore income, dividends, and capital gains for 20 years from incorporation; no alternative classification election is available under the International Companies Act 1987.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 of annual taxable supplies in Samoa
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa mandates electronic filing and payment through the Revenue Information Management System (RIMS); VAGST returns and tax clearance are submitted electronically, and registered businesses must use approved cash registers/invoicing systems that generate real-time fiscal audit records. No standalone national e-invoicing clearance or digital stamping platform is operative.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of exported tangible goods and supplies of services to non-residents (or to a business carried on outside Samoa) are zero-rated if the direct benefit occurs overseas and the supplier retains documentary proof; an International Company may claim 0% VAGST only if it has registered voluntarily for VAGST and has an approved tax-exemption status for offshore transactions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of offshore payment settlement
Samoa International Company tax exemption certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: VAGST zero-rating claims are audited by the Ministry for Revenue with revocation of the export certificate, reassessment for full VAGST plus 50% penalty and late-payment interest, and criminal prosecution (fines up to WST 20,000 and imprisonment) for fraudulent export documentation or unrepatriated sale proceeds within the deadline.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), Apia, established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984; sole monetary authority with licensing and supervisory power over all Samoan domestic commercial banks, and the statutory administrator of the Exchange Control Act 1976, the Exchange Control Regulations (as amended), and the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007; the CBS also hosts the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit for AML/CFT supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) operates a managed float anchored to a NZD/AUD/USD basket; current-account payments for goods and services are convertible through licensed dealer banks as CBS delegates, whereas capital-account transactions (portfolio transfers, offshore lending, and resident dividend remittances) require prior CBS approval unless the transactor is expressly exempt. A Samoan International Company incorporated under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended) holds non-resident status and is expressly exempt from the Exchange Control Act 1976; it therefore enjoys unrestricted current- and capital-account convertibility, may retain USD/EUR subscription revenue offshore indefinitely, and may remit dividends or repay shareholder debt without CBS licensing, provided it conducts no business with Samoan residents and executes no WST-denominated resident transactions. The practical friction point is bank-side: any Samoan licensed bank will still require an enhanced due-diligence file, a non-resident declaration, and a source-of-funds questionnaire before honouring conversion or outbound transfer instructions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Resident exporters are required to repatriate export proceeds to a licensed Samoan bank within the period fixed by CBS notice (customarily 30 days from receipt) and to convert a prescribed ratio into WST (CBS practice historically up to 50%), with certification on CBS-prescribed forms and waiver or extension available on application. The subject International Company is carved out: it is non-resident, it exports invisible digital SaaS analytics services (ISIC 6201), and it is exempt from the Exchange Control Act 1976; accordingly, no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation certificate applies, and all Stripe/Paddle settlement revenue may be held offshore in USD or EUR without Samoan conversion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD multicurrency) and Capital Escrow Account via head-office corporate banking desk
Operational Account (WST/USD); escrowed capital-injection facility available
Operational Account (WST-dominant, limited USD capability); no dedicated escrow product for non-resident ICs

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for non-Samoan digital EMIs (Mercury, Relay, Airwallex, Wise Business, Payoneer) as the primary operating treasury where the IC presents a licensed-agent incumbency certificate, discloses the true beneficial owner, and evidences an operational MarTech SaaS footprint; Medium feasibility for EMI-provided treasury functions such as lending and structured FX; Low feasibility for any WST-denominated service because foreign EMIs hold no Samoan licence. Legal constraints: (i) Samoa IC statute preserves shareholder confidentiality and authorises nominee structures, but US OCC/Fed, UK FCA, and EU EBA KYC rules require transparent UBO disclosure, a source-of-funds narrative, and proof of substance (domain ownership, cloud billing, subscriber data, payroll); (ii) a zero-tax Pacific IC with dormant accounts is commonly declined, so the underlying Stripe/Paddle revenue trail must be documentary; (iii) foreign EMIs are neither registered nor supervised by the CBS, so only their home-jurisdiction licences govern settlement; (iv) the IC redomiciliation right under Samoan law is viewed favourably by EMIs for continuity risk. Commercial recommendation: anchor one USD EMI settlement account directly to the Stripe/Paddle payout rails and maintain BSP Samoa solely for statutory and episodic compliance proof.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No Samoan statute mandates physical director attendance; the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and CBS AML/CFT rules permit risk-based remote onboarding, and current bank practice differentiates as follows: BSP and Samoa Commercial Bank accept remote account opening with a live video interview of the UBO or signing director, a certified board resolution, an agent incumbency certificate, and an in-branch attestation executed by the licensed Samoan registered agent; National Bank of Samoa commonly insists on physical appearance in Apia by at least one director or a notarially appointed attorney-in-fact. Where the IC is newly incorporated, banks classify it as an enhanced-risk client and additionally request passport and address proof for all directors, an extract of the register of directors and members, a business-profile narrative, and a completed CBS beneficial-ownership schedule kept by the registered agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt non-resident IC with no audited financial statements and an unexplained paid-in capital surge shortly after incorporation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified board resolution allocating the capital injection; issued share certificates; 3-year revenue projections; Stripe/Paddle settlement reports or executed SaaS subscription agreements; the Samoan annual return showing paid-up capital; and a registered-agent compliance certificate confirming the beneficial-ownership register

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee shareholder chain creating beneficial-ownership opacity, typical of traditional Chinese-clientele family-trust structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Agent incumbency certificate; nominee declaration with signed UBO attestation; corporate organigram linking the UBO through the nominee or trust; UBO passport and utility-bill proof of address; trust deed and current trustee resolution where a family trust sits atop the IC

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment flows touching high-risk jurisdictions or sanctioned-adjacent IP addresses
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Platform geo-blocking and anti-abuse policy; customer jurisdiction heat-map exported from the analytics tool; IP and chargeback forensic report; OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening procedure; written representation that the product is a SaaS analytics tool without payment-intermediary, crypto, or gambling functionality

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual-only operations with the registered agent address as the sole corporate location
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Co-working or development-team lease agreement; AWS/Google Cloud infrastructure invoices; employee and contractor contracts; domain-registrar ownership proof; and a monthly operating-expense trail evidencing payroll and hosting burn

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Licence Renewal Filing (International Company Annual Renewal Form)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary date of incorporation each year; renewal must be completed before the anniversary to avoid late fees.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment penalty of WST 100 (approx. USD 37) for up to 90 days; thereafter the Registrar may serve a strike-off notice and dissolve the company after a further 30 days. A struck-off company may be restored only by court order with payment of all arrears and penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (attached to annual renewal filing where a change in ownership or control has occurred)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Submitted with the Annual Licence Renewal or within 21 days after the end of the month in which any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership occurs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file a required UBO update is an offence under the International Companies (Amendment) Act; default fines up to WST 1,000 (approx. USD 370) may be imposed, with continued non-compliance leading to register strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory audit exists for ordinary Samoa International Companies. An independent audit is mandatory only where the company's constitution requires it, the directors or shareholders holding at least 10% of voting rights request it, or the company holds a banking, insurance, or trust licence containing audited financial statement obligations.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted under the International Financial Reporting Standards (voluntary adoption); the board may alternatively select any recognised foreign GAAP (e.g., US GAAP or UK GAAP). No financial statements need to be filed with the Registrar.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The International Company must maintain a Beneficial Ownership Register at its registered office. The resident agent is obligated to verify and retain supporting documents. On every annual renewal, the directors must confirm in writing that the beneficial ownership information remains accurate; any shareholding transfer or UBO change must be recorded and filed with the Registrar within 21 days of the month end. There is no separate public UBO return.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable for exempt standard International Company; if a voluntary audit is commissioned, typical fee ranges from USD 2,500 to USD 5,000 depending on transaction volume and the selected audit firm.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% (International Company full income tax exemption); Samoa domestic corporate income tax headline rate: 27%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory exemption from income tax, capital gains tax, and all distributions for 20 years from incorporation, renewable with SIFA approval; no withholding tax on IC dividends, interest, or royalties; no stamp duty on IC instruments; no exchange control restrictions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: SIFA Annual Return (International Company) — prescribed form under the International Companies Act 1987, filed through the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) online e-filing portal by a SIFA-licensed registered agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 30 days of each anniversary of the date of incorporation, together with the annual government fee (WST-based fee scale keyed to issued share capital).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 — Company Name and Registration Number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full legal name of the International Company and the unique SIFA registration number as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must match the Certificate of Incorporation exactly; non-resident owners must file through their licensed registered agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical address of the registered office in Samoa maintained by the licensed registered agent; a P.O. Box is insufficient.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory for all ICs regardless of the residence of shareholders; a Samoan physical address must be maintained at all times.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and SIFA license number of the registered agent acting for the International Company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs must retain a SIFA-licensed agent in Samoa; change of agent must be notified within 14 days.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full names, nationalities, and addresses of all directors and of the secretary; directors must be natural persons and no Samoan residency requirement applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Corporate directors are not permitted for ICs; non-resident individuals may serve as directors.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 — Share Capital and Beneficial Owners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classes and number of issued shares, par value, shareholder names, and ultimate beneficial owner declaration; bearer shares are prohibited.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Full UBO disclosure is mandatory for non-resident shareholders; incomplete disclosure triggers AML non-compliance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 — Tax Status and Domestic Business Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the IC is not carrying on business in Samoa with Samoan residents, which would forfeit exempt status, and declaration of any economic substance category under the ESR.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs must confirm all trading is offshore; any on-island revenue subjects the IC to Samoa income tax and VAGST.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing after the 30-day window attracts a late penalty of WST 500. Non-payment of the annual fee for 90 days after the anniversary: the Registrar may strike the IC off the register and dissolve it without further notice; restoration requires arrears, a reinstatement fee, and, after 12 months, a court order. Knowingly false statements in the annual return attract a fine up to WST 100,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Economic Substance Notification (ESN) — filed with SIFA through the registered agent under the International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations 2019.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 12 months of the end of the IC's financial year, or on the date directed by SIFA; a separate notification of the relevant activity must be filed within 30 days of commencement of the activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selection of the ESR category: for the SEO content analytics SaaS, 'Intellectual Property Business' or 'Distribution and Service Centre Business' is applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The IC must identify the activity giving rise to income; offshore management alone does not satisfy the category.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from the relevant activity and operating expenditure incurred, segregated by jurisdiction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ICs must disclose the source jurisdiction of all SaaS subscription and analytics license income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Number of full-time employees in Samoa and the physical premises (owned or leased) from which core income-generating activities are performed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Employees must be physically present in Samoa; remote foreign contractors do not count toward substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation of board meetings held in Samoa, quorum at each meeting, minutes kept in Samoa, and strategic decisions made by the Samoan board.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Meeting records and electronic minutes must be maintained in Samoa and produced to SIFA on demand.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the ESN: penalty up to WST 100,000. Failure of the economic substance test: penalty up to WST 500,000, exchange of information reporting, and possible strike-off; directors and registered agents may be fined and disqualified.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for International Company distributions (exempt under the International Companies Act 1987, s.193). Samoa's general non-resident dividend withholding tax rate under the Income Tax Act 2007 is 15% for dividends paid by taxable domestic resident companies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Not required for IC distributions because no withholding tax is levied. For taxable domestic dividends, the beneficial owner must (1) obtain a Certificate of Residence (TRC) from its home jurisdiction, (2) submit the prescribed non-resident withholding tax relief declaration form to the payer and to Samoa's Ministry of Revenue before payment, and (3) satisfy any limitation-of-benefits and beneficial ownership clauses under the applicable DTA. Samoa's relevant DTAs are the Samoa–China DTA (signed 2020, entered into force 2021) and the Samoa–New Zealand DTA, both providing reduced rates: dividends 5%/15%, interest 10%, royalties 10%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-resident withholding tax: interest 15%, royalties 15% (Income Tax Act 2007); payments made by an International Company are exempt from withholding tax. Treaty rates: interest 10% and royalties 10% under both the Samoa–China DTA and the Samoa–New Zealand DTA.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Not applicable — Samoa imposes no statutory Local File or Master File filing thresholds. The arm's length principle applies under the Income Tax Act 2007 to taxable resident companies, but the tax-exempt IC has no income tax transfer pricing filing duty. For ESR purposes, an IP-rich IC must retain contemporaneous evidence of intercompany pricing for SaaS/IP royalties and service fees, including contracts, comparability analysis, cost allocations, headcount, and expenditure in Samoa. Where Stripe or Paddle act as merchant of record or payment facilitator, the fees paid to them and the residual SaaS/IP revenue allocated to the IC must be documented as arm's length.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies (Economic Substance) Regulations 2019, in force since 1 January 2020, require every IC undertaking a relevant activity — including Intellectual Property Business and Distribution and Service Centre Business — to demonstrate in Samoa: (a) core income-generating activities performed by qualified full-time employees; (b) adequate physical premises; (c) adequate operating expenditure in Samoa; and (d) board meetings and strategic management conducted in Samoa. A pure equity holding IC must maintain employees and premises adequate for holding the equity interest. The SEO content analytics SaaS tool constitutes an IP asset; income from its licensing, subscriptions, and analytics must be justified by economic substance in Samoa, failing which the IC will be deemed non-compliant and reported to international authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SEO analytics SaaS as an IP-holding IC with no employees, premises, board presence, or decision-making in Samoa; filing false economic substance notifications; outsourcing all core revenue-generating activities to foreign affiliates; routing subscription collections solely through foreign payment processors such as Stripe and Paddle without any Samoan operational presence; failing to file the annual ESN.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty up to WST 500,000 for failing the economic substance test; penalty up to WST 100,000 for failure to file the ESN; strike-off and dissolution by SIFA; revocation of the 20-year tax exemption; automatic exchange of information reporting to foreign tax authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers may be fined up to WST 100,000, disqualified from acting as directors for up to 5 years, and, for fraudulent declarations, imprisoned up to 5 years; civil restitution may be ordered against directors who benefited from the non-compliant structure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to disclose the ultimate beneficial owner to the registered agent; maintaining nominee chains used to conceal ownership; processing payments through unreported accounts; the registered agent's failure to conduct customer due diligence under Samoa's Financial Intelligence Unit regime.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalties up to WST 1,000,000; forfeiture and freezing orders under the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit framework; criminal money laundering conviction carries imprisonment up to 14 years; the IC may be struck off and its assets vested in the Government of Samoa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors knowingly involved in money laundering face imprisonment up to 14 years, personal criminal fines, travel bans pending investigation, and confiscation of personal assets; directors may also be barred from holding office in any Samoa company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Breach of Tax-Exempt Status
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling SEO analytics subscriptions to Samoa-resident customers, maintaining a fixed base in Samoa, or otherwise conducting domestic business, without registration for income tax and VAGST; making false declarations to preserve the exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of the exemption with back assessment of income tax at 27%, VAGST at 15%, and interest; evasion penalties up to 150% of the tax shortfall; criminal fine up to WST 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed false declarations or knowingly benefited from the evasion are jointly and severally liable for the assessed taxes and penalties; convicted directors face imprisonment up to 5 years and are disqualified from managing companies in Samoa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-payment of the annual government fee or failure to file the annual return within 30 days of the incorporation anniversary; continuing to trade after dissolution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late penalty of WST 500; strike-off and dissolution after 90 days of default; assets of the struck-off IC automatically vest in the Government of Samoa; restoration requires arrears, reinstatement fees, and, if more than 12 months have elapsed, a court order.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Upon strike-off, the corporate veil is pierced: directors and shareholders are personally liable for debts incurred after dissolution; transacting in the dissolved company's name is a criminal offense punishable by fine and imprisonment up to 2 years.
